title: airgapped-deployments-procurement-playbook
body:
Executive summary:

This is a playbook for GTM and field teams when engaging regulated buyers who require air-gapped or fully-offline/private deployments. Focus is on procurement and legal friction, control plane topology options, and pragmatic rebuttals to common objections. The goal: move conversations from abstract security concerns to concrete acceptance criteria and an executable procurement package.

Primary audience:
- Procurement leads, security and compliance (CISO, Head of InfoSec)
- Platform engineering and infra buyers
- Legal / contracts teams evaluating SLAs and liabilities

Core positioning statements (short form):
- "Redwood provides a production-grade inference platform that can run entirely within your network boundaries—no egress, no shared control plane—while preserving product parity with our hosted API."
- "We partner on validated installation and hand-off, and include a controlled upgrade path and audit-ready telemetry that you keep."
- "Risk transfer is explicit: we operationalize deployment, you retain custody of data and keys."

Elevator (30–60s):
- Problem: Regulated orgs cannot accept callouts to external control planes or unknown telemetry flows.
- Redwood: flexible control-plane models (local-only, split-control with no-data-egress, managed-but-airgapped) that are audited, documented, and contractually enforced.
- Benefit: speed of adoption without long rebuilds—same inference APIs, enterprise-grade throughput, and support SLAs suitable for production workloads.

Control plane topologies (plain-language):
1) Fully-local control plane (recommended for highest regulatory parity)
   - All services (control plane, model repository, metrics, upgrade artifacts) live in-customer network or airgapped environment.
   - Redwood provides an installation bundle + runbook and optional on-site validation.
   - Security posture: customer keys never leave KMS; telemetry is stored locally.

2) Split control plane (most pragmatic for enterprises with strict boundaries)
   - Customer runs runtime + model storage locally; Redwood-hosted control plane handles billing and entitlement metadata via a narrow, one-way, customer-initiated token exchange or offline attestation protocol.
   - No customer data or requests are transmitted; only metadata hash + install fingerprints.

3) Managed-offline (for customers who want Redwood to operate but maintain custody)
   - Periodic physical media updates or secure pull from an approved mirror.
   - Redwood operates under a site-ops SLA and on-site engineers during onboarding phases.

Packaging for procurement (what to include in the RFP response / SOW):
- Technical Annex: component list, port maps, firewall rules, minimum hardware matrix (GPU/CPU, memory, disk), and sample sizing for QPS.
- Security Annex: data flow diagrams, KMS/HSM integration patterns, threat model summary, and audit log retention options.
- Delivery & Acceptance Criteria: installation validation plan, performance baseline test (latency/throughput per corridor), and operational runbook hand-off.
- SLAs & Support: targeted MTTR for on-site vs remote, patch cadence, emergency security fix process, and optional on-prem concierge.
- Liability & Data Custody clause language: explicit statements that customer retains custody of PII and model inputs/outputs; Redwood's role limited to software and operational process as defined.

Common buyer objections and suggested rebuttals (script snippets):
1) "We can't have any external control plane because of audit."
   - Rebuttal: "We offer a fully-local control plane option. We'll include an audit checklist and the signed SOW will guarantee zero egress of runtime traffic; our acceptance tests will be run in your environment so you can validate."

2) "How do you handle upgrades without internet?"
   - Rebuttal: "We support signed release bundles delivered via secure transfer or pulled from a customer-approved mirror; upgrades can be staged and applied by your team or by Redwood under an on-site upgrade window."

3) "What about telemetry/phone-home behavior?"
   - Rebuttal: "Telemetry is configurable: default is local-only. Any telemetry that leaves the environment is explicitly documented and requires admin opt-in. Our config and runbooks make this repeatable."

4) "If something breaks, who is accountable?"
   - Rebuttal: "Operational responsibility is codified in the SOW: Redwood will remediate code defects and provide troubleshooting; the customer operates infrastructure and can elect concierge support for deeper ops assistance with defined escalation paths."

Competitive mapping (concise):
- Competitor A (managed-hosted): fast time-to-value but fails for air-gapped buyers. Use our airgapped messaging to win when the buyer's non-negotiable is data residency.
- Competitor B (OSS runtime + integrator): can be low cost but lacks operational SLAs, hardened installation, and vendor-backed liability language—ours is a middle path: pre-integrated runtime + vendor accountability.
- Competitor C (enterprise appliance vendors): may provide strict isolation but often lack inference runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache, quantization switches) and modern rollout tooling—highlight Redwood's runtime parity with hosted product.

Proof points & technical artifacts to show: (attach these to RFP response)
- On-site acceptance test report template (latency/throughput/99thp metrics).
- Example audit log extract (sanitized) demonstrating local retention and log format.
- Architecture diagram for fully-local and split models (Confluence page linked).
- Reference customer: legal-approved quote + short anonymized case study (if available).

Procurement play actions (field checklist):
- Day 0: collect compliance questionnaire, architecture diagram, and compliance-required contact list.
- Day 3: deliver Technical Annex and Security Annex draft.
- Day 7: schedule architecture walkthrough with customer infra and security.
- Day 10–14: produce SOW and acceptance criteria; propose a pilot window.
- Pilot: run acceptance test in customer environment, collect signed runbook.

Pricing and packaging notes (conversation starters for AE):
- Baseline: on-prem software license + 12-month support (includes security patches).
- Optional: concierge deployment (fixed-fee professional services) and annual on-site health checks.
- Billing model: subscription for software & support; hardware procurement is typically passed through or recommended partners listed.

Legal & contract flags to escalate to legal: 
- Any demand for vendor indemnities beyond industry norms (engineering to legal).
- Requests to retain keys or decrypt telemetry (security to legal).
- Requirements for unredacted source access or permanent code escrow—handle case-by-case with legal.

Samples (quick scripts):
- CISO opening line: "We need a deployment that never leaves our network and provides auditable evidence of that. Can you show a step-by-step plan?"
- AE reply: "Yes — we have three validated deployment topologies. The quickest path is split-control for low friction; for no-egress requirements, we’ll propose a fully-local bundle and an on-site acceptance plan."

Open questions / engineering dependencies for sales to clear before committing:
- Which release channels will be used for airgapped customers and what is the signed-release verification process? (ENG input required)
- Backup / DR patterns: customer expectations for model snapshot replication and restore windows.
- Minimum validated hardware matrix: need explicit AMD/NVIDIA GPU families and driver versions.

Next steps (internal):
- Convert this playbook into a concise one-pager for AE toolkit and a separate technical annex template.
- Align legal on standard SOW language for custody, upgrades, and liability for airgapped installs.
- Build an "airgap kit" zip with pre-approved signed bundles, install scripts, and an acceptance test harness.

Notes to self / loose ideas (working):
- Consider a short checklist that can be completed in a 1hr kickoff to rapidly qualify whether split-control is acceptable vs fully-local.
- Investigate a signed attestation flow that gives Redwood visibility into entitlement without showing customer data (helps billing without egress).
- Add a customer-facing FAQ and a one-page exec briefing for procurement committees.

References: see linked artifacts and PD-4182 for the current roadmap items that unblock a fully managed offline offering.

-- END --
